fun struct structName => do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM Unit := fun __r => do
    let __x ← Lean.getConstInfo structName
    match __x with
      | Lean.ConstantInfo.inductInfo val =>
        if (val.levelParams.isEmpty && val.numIndices == 0 && val.numParams == 0) = true then
          pure ()
        else
          Lean.throwErrorAt struct.raw
            (Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName structName) ++
              Lean.toMessageData "` must not have parameters, indices, or universe parameters")
      | x =>
        Lean.throwErrorAt struct.raw
          (Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName structName) ++
            Lean.toMessageData "` is not a structure")
  if Lean.isStructure env structName = true then __do_jp ()
    else do
      let __r ←
        Lean.throwErrorAt struct.raw
            (Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName structName) ++
              Lean.toMessageData "` is not a structure")
      __do_jp __r

  let s ← get
  match
      Array.findIdx?
        (fun x =>
          match x with
          | (fst, name) => name == key)
        (Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.State.toOmit✝ s) with
    | some idx =>
      match (Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.State.toOmit✝ s)[idx]! with
      | (ref, snd) => do
        Lean.Elab.addConstInfo ref.raw projFn
        set
            { toDerive := Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.State.toDerive✝ s,
              toOmit := (Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.State.toOmit✝ s).eraseIdx! idx }
        pure true
    | x => pure false

doc:
Trie used to organize those handlers provided in `EvalConfigItemView` and those
handlers that are synthesized.

The fields in this `structure` are given in the order they are applied.
Conceptually, searching for handlers is done recursively (however the algorithm is compiled
into non-recursive code via metaprogramming). At each step of the search the state
consists of a trie key `tkey`, a trie node `trie`, and a configuration key `ckey`.
Once any handler is applied, matching is complete (handlers can't decide not to apply at run time).
1. If `exact?` is present and `tkey == ckey`, then it is applied.
2. If `ckey` is of the form `root.ckey'` and there's a `(root, trie')` entry in `children`,
   then we recursively search for a handler using `tkey.root`, `trie'`, `ckey'`.
   If one is found, it is applied.
3. If `wildcard?` is present and `ckey'` is nonempty, then that handler is applied.
4. Otherwise, the search failed. If this is recursive, we return and continue.

fun optionPrefix opts item =>
  have optName := optionPrefix ++ item.getCurrOptionName;
  do
  Lean.Elab.addCompletionInfo
      (Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.option
        (Lean.mkNullNode #[item.prevRoot, Lean.mkNullNode item.optionComps.toArray]))
  let decl ← liftM (Lean.getOptionDecl optName)
  Lean.Elab.pushInfoLeaf
      (Lean.Elab.Info.ofOptionInfo
        { stx := item.option.raw, optionName := optName, declName := decl.declName })
  have set :
    (α : Type) →
      [Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.EvalTerm α] →
        [Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.EvalExpr α] →
          [Lean.KVMap.Value α] → Lean.Elab.TermElabM Lean.Options :=
    fun α [Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.EvalTerm α] [Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.EvalExpr α]
      [Lean.KVMap.Value α] =>
    do
    let value ← Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.evalTermOrExprWithElab { raw := item.value }
    pure (opts.set optName value)
  match decl.defValue with
    | Lean.DataValue.ofBool v => set Bool
    | Lean.DataValue.ofNat v => do
      item.checkNotBool
      set ℕ
    | Lean.DataValue.ofInt v => do
      item.checkNotBool
      set ℤ
    | Lean.DataValue.ofString v => do
      item.checkNotBool
      set String
    | Lean.DataValue.ofName v => do
      item.checkNotBool
      set Lean.Name
    | Lean.DataValue.ofSyntax v =>
      Lean.throwErrorAt item.option.raw
        (Lean.toMessageData "Cannot set `Syntax` option `" ++ Lean.toMessageData optName ++
          Lean.toMessageData "`")

fun simpArgs usedSimps =>

          have mask := __s;
          match simpArgs[i] with
          | (ref, arg) =>
            have __do_jp := fun used =>
              have mask := mask.push used;
              pure (ForInStep.yield mask);
            match arg with
            | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.addEntries entries => do

                    (fun x =>
                      match x with
                      | Lean.Meta.SimpEntry.thm thm => do
                        let __do_lift ←
                          Lean.Elab.Tactic.warnUnusedSimpArgs.usedThmIdOfSimpTheorem✝ thm
                        pure (usedSimps.contains __do_lift)
                      | Lean.Meta.SimpEntry.toUnfold declName =>
                        pure (usedSimps.contains (Lean.Meta.Origin.decl declName))
                      | Lean.Meta.SimpEntry.toUnfoldThms _declName thms =>
                        pure (thms.any fun x => usedSimps.contains (Lean.Meta.Origin.decl x)))

              __do_jp used
            | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.addSimproc declName post => do
              let used ← pure (usedSimps.contains (Lean.Meta.Origin.decl declName post))
              __do_jp used
            | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.addLetToUnfold fvarId => do
              let used ← pure (usedSimps.contains (Lean.Meta.Origin.fvar fvarId))
              __do_jp used

              let used ← pure true
              __do_jp used
            | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.eraseSimproc toErase => do
              let used ← pure true
              __do_jp used
            | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.ext ext₁? ext₂? h => do
              let used ← pure true
              __do_jp used
            | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.star => do
              let used ← pure true

`simpLocation ctx discharge? varIdToLemmaId loc`
runs the simplifier at locations specified by `loc`,
using the simp theorems collected in `ctx`
optionally running a discharger specified in `discharge?` on generated subgoals.

Its primary use is as the implementation of the
`simp [...] at ...` and `simp only [...] at ...` syntaxes,
but can also be used by other tactics when a `Syntax` is not available.

For many tactics other than the simplifier,
one should use the `withLocation` tactic combinator
when working with a `location`.

doc:
Implement a `simp` discharge function using the given tactic syntax code.
Recall that `simp` dischargers are in `SimpM` which does not have access to `Term.State`.
We need access to `Term.State` to store messages and update the info tree.
Thus, we create an `IO.ref` to track these changes at `Term.State` when we execute `tacticCode`.
We must set this reference with the current `Term.State` before we execute `simp` using the
generated `Simp.Discharge`.

  Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM (IO.Ref Lean.Elab.Term.State × Lean.Meta.Simp.Discharge)

fun tacticCode => do
  let tacticCode ←
    do
      let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
      let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
      let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
      pure
          {
            raw :=
              Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticTry_ (Lean.Syntax.atom info "try")
                (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq
                  (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq1Indented
                    (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `null
                      (Lean.Syntax.node3 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.paren (Lean.Syntax.atom info "(")
                        { raw := tacticCode }.raw (Lean.Syntax.atom info ")"))))) }
  let __do_lift ← getThe Lean.Elab.Term.State
  let ref ← liftM (IO.mkRef __do_lift)
  let ctx ← readThe Lean.Elab.Term.Context
  have disch : Lean.Meta.Simp.Discharge := fun e => do
    let mvar ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprSyntheticOpaqueMVar e `simp.discharger)
    let s ← ST.Ref.get ref
    have runTac? : Lean.Elab.TermElabM (Option Lean.Expr) := do
      let e ←
        tryCatch
            (do
              let r ←
                Lean.Elab.Term.withoutModifyingElabMetaStateWithInfo do
                    Lean.Elab.Term.withSynthesize
                        (Lean.Elab.Term.runTactic mvar.mvarId! tacticCode.raw
                          Lean.Elab.Term.TacticMVarKind.term false)
                    let result ← Lean.instantiateMVars mvar
                    if result.hasExprMVar = true then pure none else pure (some result)
              ExceptT.run (pure r))
            fun x => EarlyReturnT.return none
      EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r
    let __x ← liftM (runTac?.run ctx s)
    match __x with
      | (result?, s) => do
        ST.Ref.set ref s
        pure result?
  pure (ref, disch)

            have args := #[];

                  have starArg := __s.1;
                  have args := __s.2;

                    Lean.Elab.Tactic.elabSimpArg✝ ctx.indexConfig (eraseLocal || starArg) kind
                        argStx

                        match arg with
                        | Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult.star => true
                        | x => false)

                    args.push (argStx, arg)

            have args : Array (Lean.Syntax × Lean.Elab.Tactic.ElabSimpArgResult) := __s.2
            have thmsArray : Lean.Meta.SimpTheoremsArray := ctx.simpTheorems
            have thms : Lean.Meta.SimpTheorems := thmsArray[0]!
            have simprocs : Lean.Meta.Simp.SimprocsArray := simprocs

              forIn args (thmsArray, thms, simprocs) fun x __s =>
                  have thmsArray := __s.1;
                  have __s := __s.2;
                  have thms := __s.1;
                  have simprocs := __s.2;

                            have thms := thms.addSimpEntry entry;
                            pure (ForInStep.yield thms)

                    have mvs0 := Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.TacticData.goalsTargetedBy✝ td;
                    have mvs1 := Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.TacticData.goalsCreatedBy✝ td;
                    have skind := s.getKind;
                    if Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.stoppers✝.contains skind = true then
                      pure (ForInStep.yield (stains, msgs))
                    else
                      have shouldStain? :=
                        Mathlib.Linter.flexible?✝ s && mvs1.length == mvs0.length;
                      do
                      let __s ←
                        forIn (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.getStained!✝ s) (stains, msgs) fun d __s =>
                            have stains := __s.1;
                            have msgs := __s.2;
                            have __do_jp := fun __r stains msgs =>
                              have new := #[];
                              do
                              let __s ←
                                forIn stains new fun x __s =>
                                    have new := __s;
                                    match x with
                                    | (fv, stainData) =>
                                      have psisted :=
                                        Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.reallyPersist✝ #[fv] mvs0 mvs1 ctx0
                                          ctx1;
                                      have __do_jp := fun __r new => do
                                        let __s ←
                                          forIn psisted new fun p __s =>
                                              have new := __s;
                                              have new := new.push (p, stainData);
                                              pure (ForInStep.yield new)
                                        have new :
                                          Array
                                            ((Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) ×
                                              Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) :=
                                          __s
                                        pure (ForInStep.yield new);
                                      if (psisted == #[] && mvs1 != []) = true then
                                        have new := new.push (fv, stainData);
                                        dbgTrace
                                          (toString "lost " ++
                                            toString
                                              ((fv.1.name, fv.2.name),
                                                Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.stained✝
                                                  stainData,
                                                Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.stx✝ stainData))
                                          fun x => __do_jp () new
                                      else __do_jp () new
                              have new :
                                Array
                                  ((Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) ×
                                    Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) :=
                                __s
                              have stains :
                                Array
                                  ((Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) ×
                                    Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) :=
                                new
                              pure (ForInStep.yield (stains, msgs));
                            if shouldStain? = true then do
                              let __s ←
                                forIn mvs1 stains fun currMVar1 __s =>
                                    have stains := __s;
                                    have lctx1 := (ctx1.decls.findD currMVar1 default).lctx;
                                    have locsAfter :=
                                      Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.Stained.toFMVarId✝ currMVar1 lctx1 d;
                                    have stainData :=
                                      { stained := d, stx := s,
                                        ci := Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.TacticData.ci✝ td,
                                        mctx := ctx0, goals := mvs0 };
                                    have stains :=
                                      stains ++ Array.map (fun l => (l, stainData)) locsAfter;
                                    pure (ForInStep.yield stains)
                              have stains :
                                Array
                                  ((Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) ×
                                    Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) :=
                                __s
                              __do_jp () stains msgs
                            else
                              have stained_in_syntax :=
                                if Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.usesGoal?✝ skind = true then
                                  (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.toStained✝ s).insert d
                                else Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.toStained✝ s;
                              if (!Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.flexible✝.contains skind) = true then do
                                let __s ←
                                  forIn mvs0 msgs fun currMv0 __s =>
                                      have msgs := __s;
                                      have lctx0 := (ctx0.decls.findD currMv0 default).lctx;
                                      have foundFvs := ∅;
                                      do
                                      let __s ←
                                        forIn stained_in_syntax foundFvs fun st __s =>
                                            have foundFvs := __s;
                                            do
                                            let __s ←
                                              forIn
                                                  (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.Stained.toFMVarId✝
                                                    currMv0 lctx0 st)
                                                  foundFvs fun d __s =>
                                                  have foundFvs := __s;
                                                  if (!foundFvs.contains d) = true then
                                                    have foundFvs := foundFvs.insert d;
                                                    pure (ForInStep.yield foundFvs)
                                                  else pure (ForInStep.yield foundFvs)
                                            have foundFvs :
                                              Std.HashSet (Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) := __s
                                            pure (ForInStep.yield foundFvs)
                                      have foundFvs : Std.HashSet (Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) := __s
                                      let __s ←
                                        forIn foundFvs msgs fun l __s =>
                                            have msgs := __s;
                                            match Array.find? (fun x => x.1 == l) stains with
                                            | some (_stdLoc, stainData) =>
                                              have msgs := msgs.push (s, stainData);
                                              pure (ForInStep.yield msgs)
                                            | x => pure (ForInStep.yield msgs)
                                      have msgs :
                                        Array (Lean.Syntax × Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) :=
                                        __s
                                      pure (ForInStep.yield msgs)
                                have msgs :
                                  Array (Lean.Syntax × Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) := __s
                                __do_jp () stains msgs
                              else __do_jp () stains msgs
                      have stains :
                        Array ((Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) × Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) :=
                        __s.1
                      have msgs : Array (Lean.Syntax × Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) := __s.2
                      pure (ForInStep.yield (stains, msgs))
              have stains :
                Array ((Lean.FVarId × Lean.MVarId) × Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) := __s.1
              have msgs : Array (Lean.Syntax × Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData✝) := __s.2
              forIn msgs PUnit.unit fun x __s =>
                  match x with
                  | (s, stainData) =>
                    have stainStx := Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.stx✝ stainData;
                    have d := Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.stained✝ stainData;
                    have stainStr := (stainStx.reprint.getD (toString stainStx)).trimAscii;
                    do
                    let suggestion? ←
                      Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM
                          (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.generateSimpSuggestion✝ stainData stainStx)
                    have msg : Lean.MessageData :=
                      match stainStx.getKind with
                      | `Lean.Parser.Tactic.simp =>
                        match d with
                        | Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.Stained.wildcard✝ =>
                          Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData stainStr ++
                            Lean.toMessageData
                              "` is a flexible tactic that potentially modifies all hypotheses and the current goal with a wildcard `*`. Try `simp?` and use the suggested `simp only [...]`. Alternatively, use `suffices` to explicitly state the simplified form."
                        | x =>
                          Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData stainStr ++
                                Lean.toMessageData "` is a flexible tactic modifying `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData d ++
                            Lean.toMessageData
                              "`. Try `simp?` and use the suggested `simp only [...]`. Alternatively, use `suffices` to explicitly state the simplified form."
                      | `Lean.Parser.Tactic.simpAll =>
                        Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData stainStr ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "` is a flexible tactic modifying `" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData d ++
                          Lean.toMessageData
                            "`. Try `simp_all?` and use the suggested `simp_all only [...]`. Alternatively, use `suffices` to explicitly state the simplified form."
                      | `Aesop.Frontend.Parser.aesopTactic =>
                        Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData stainStr ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "` is a flexible tactic modifying `" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData d ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "`. Try `aesop?` and use the suggested proof."
                      | x =>
                        Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData stainStr ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "` is a flexible tactic modifying `" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData d ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "`."
                    Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.flexible stainStx msg
                    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Command.CommandElabM (ForInStep PUnit.{1}) :=
                      fun __r => do
                      let fm ← Lean.getFileMap
                      have stainLine? : Option ℕ :=
                        Option.map (Lean.Position.line ∘ fm.toPosition) stainStx.getPos?
                      have lineStr : Lean.MessageData :=
                        match stainLine? with
                        | some line =>
                          (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                            (toString " on line " ++ toString line)
                        | x => (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) ""
                      have atomStr : Lean.MessageData :=
                        match stainStx[0] with
                        | Lean.Syntax.atom info val =>
                          (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "the flexible tactic " ++
                            (Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData val ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "`")
                        | x => (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "a flexible tactic"
                      Lean.logInfoAt s
                          (match d with
                          | Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.Stained.name✝ a =>
                            Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofSyntax s).group ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData "`\nuses `" ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData d ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData "`, which was modified by " ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData atomStr ++
                                Lean.toMessageData lineStr ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "!"
                          | Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.Stained.goal✝ =>
                            Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofSyntax s).group ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData
                                      "`\nmodifies the current goal, which was modified by " ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData atomStr ++
                                Lean.toMessageData lineStr ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "!"
                          | Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.Stained.wildcard✝ =>
                            Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofSyntax s).group ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData "`\nuses a rigid tactic. Previously, " ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData atomStr ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                    ", which potentially modified all hypotheses and the goal with a wildcard `*`, was used" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData lineStr ++
                              Lean.toMessageData ".")
                      pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                    match suggestion? with
                      | some suggStx => do
                        let __r ←
                          Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM
                              (Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.addSuggestion stainStx
                                {
                                  suggestion :=
                                    Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.SuggestionText.tsyntax
                                      { raw := suggStx } }
                                (some stainStx))
                        __do_jp __r
                      | x => __do_jp ()
              pure ()
        else pure (),
  name :=
    (((((((((Lean.Name.anonymous.mkStr "_private").mkStr "Mathlib").mkStr "Tactic").mkStr
                              "Linter").mkStr
                          "FlexibleLinter").mkNum
                      0).mkStr
                  "Mathlib").mkStr
              "Linter").mkStr
          "Flexible").mkStr
      "flexibleLinter" }

doc:
Generate a "simp only [...]" suggestion for a simp/simpAll tactic.
Returns `none` if the tactic is not simp/simpAll or if suggestion generation fails.

value.text:
fun stainData stainStx =>
  match stainStx.getKind with
  | `Lean.Parser.Tactic.simp => do
    let e ←
      tryCatch
          (match (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.goals✝ stainData)[0]? with
          | some mv =>
            match (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.mctx✝ stainData).decls.find? mv with
            | some mvDecl => do
              let r ←
                liftM
                    ((Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.ci✝ stainData).runMetaM mvDecl.lctx
                      (Lean.Meta.withMCtx (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.mctx✝ stainData) do
                        let ctx ← Lean.Meta.Simp.Context.mkDefault
                        let simprocs ← liftM Lean.Meta.Simp.getSimprocs
                        let __x ← Lean.Meta.simpGoal mv ctx #[simprocs]
                        match __x with
                          | (fst, stats) =>
                            if Lean.PersistentHashMap.isEmpty stats.usedTheorems.map = true then
                              pure none
                            else do
                              let suggStx ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.mkSimpOnly stainStx stats.usedTheorems
                              pure (some suggStx)))
              ExceptT.run (pure r)
            | x => EarlyReturnT.return none
          | x => EarlyReturnT.return none)
          fun x => EarlyReturnT.return none
    EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r
  | `Lean.Parser.Tactic.simpAll => do
    let e ←
      tryCatch
          (match (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.goals✝ stainData)[0]? with
          | some mv =>
            match (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.mctx✝ stainData).decls.find? mv with
            | some mvDecl => do
              let r ←
                liftM
                    ((Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.ci✝ stainData).runMetaM mvDecl.lctx
                      (Lean.Meta.withMCtx (Mathlib.Linter.Flexible.StainData.mctx✝ stainData) do
                        let ctx ← Lean.Meta.Simp.Context.mkDefault
                        let simprocs ← liftM Lean.Meta.Simp.getSimprocs
                        let __x ← Lean.Meta.simpGoal mv ctx #[simprocs]
                        match __x with
                          | (fst, stats) =>
                            if Lean.PersistentHashMap.isEmpty stats.usedTheorems.map = true then
                              pure none
                            else do
                              let suggStx ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.mkSimpOnly stainStx stats.usedTheorems
                              pure (some suggStx)))
              ExceptT.run (pure r)
            | x => EarlyReturnT.return none
          | x => EarlyReturnT.return none)
          fun x => EarlyReturnT.return none
    EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r
  | x => pure none

`getStained! stx` expects `stx` to be an argument of a node of `SyntaxNodeKind`
`Lean.Parser.Tactic.location`.
Typically, we apply `getStained!` to the output of `getLocs`.

It returns the `HashSet` of `Stained` determined by the locations in `stx`.

The only difference with `getStained stx`, is that `getStained!` never returns `{}`:
if `getStained stx = {}`, then `getStained' stx = {.goal}`.

This means that tactics that do not have an explicit "`at`" in their syntax will be treated as
acting on the main goal.

doc:
If `e` is a projection of the structure constructor, reduce the projection.
Otherwise returns `none`. If this function detects that expression is ill-typed, throws an error.
For example, given `Prod.fst (x, y)`, returns `some x`.

value.text:
fun e =>
  match e.getAppFn with
  | Lean.Expr.const cname us => do
    let __x ← Lean.getProjectionFnInfo? cname
    match __x with
      | some pinfo =>
        let args := e.getAppArgs;
        if ha : args.size = pinfo.numParams + 1 then
          have sarg := args[pinfo.numParams];
          if sarg.getAppFn.isConstOf pinfo.ctorName = true then
            have sfields := sarg.getAppArgs;
            have sidx := pinfo.numParams + pinfo.i;
            if hs : sidx < sfields.size then pure (some sfields[sidx])
            else
              Lean.throwError
                (Lean.toMessageData "ill-formed expression, " ++ Lean.toMessageData cname ++
                          Lean.toMessageData " is the " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData (pinfo.i + 1) ++
                      Lean.toMessageData "-th projection function but " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData sarg ++
                  Lean.toMessageData " does not have enough arguments")
          else pure none
        else pure none
      | x => pure none
  | x => pure none

fun e fieldName => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType e
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.whnf __do_lift
  match __do_lift.getAppFn with
    | Lean.Expr.const structName us => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
      match Lean.findField? __do_lift structName fieldName with
        | some baseStruct =>
          have e := e;
          do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
          let __s ←
            forIn (Lean.getPathToBaseStructure? __do_lift baseStruct structName).get! e
                fun projName __s =>
                have e := __s;
                do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType e
                let type ← Lean.Meta.whnf __do_lift
                match type.getAppFn with
                  | Lean.Expr.const _structName us =>
                    have e := Lean.mkAppN (Lean.Expr.const projName us) (type.getAppArgs.push e);
                    pure (ForInStep.yield e)
                  | x => do
                    Lean.throwError
                        (Lean.toMessageData e ++
                          Lean.toMessageData " doesn't have a structure as type")
                    pure (ForInStep.yield e)
          have e : Lean.Expr := __s
          e.mkDirectProjection fieldName
        | x =>
          Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "No parent of " ++ Lean.toMessageData structName ++
                Lean.toMessageData " has field " ++
              Lean.toMessageData fieldName)
    | x =>
      Lean.throwError
        (Lean.toMessageData e ++ Lean.toMessageData " doesn't have a structure as type")

doc:
A linter for checking that declarations aren't syntactic tautologies.
Checks whether a lemma is a declaration of the form `∀ a b ... z, e₁ = e₂`
where `e₁` and `e₂` are identical exprs.
We call declarations of this form syntactic tautologies.
Such lemmas are (mostly) useless and sometimes introduced unintentionally when proving basic facts
with rfl when elaboration results in a different term than the user intended.

    let __do_lift ← Batteries.Tactic.Lint.isAutoDecl declName
    if __do_lift = true then pure none
      else do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.getConstInfo declName
        Lean.Meta.forallTelescope __do_lift.type fun x ty =>
            match
              Option.map
                  (fun x =>
                    match x with
                    | (fst, l, r) => (l, r))
                  ty.eq? <|>
                ty.iff? with
            | some (lhs, rhs) =>
              if (lhs == rhs) = true then
                pure (some (Lean.toMessageData "LHS equals RHS syntactically"))
              else pure none
            | x => pure none,
  noErrorsFound :=
    (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "No declarations are syntactic tautologies.",
  errorsFound :=
    (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
      "THE FOLLOWING DECLARATIONS ARE SYNTACTIC TAUTOLOGIES. This usually means that they are of the form `∀ a b ... z, e₁ = e₂` where `e₁` and `e₂` are identical expressions. We call declarations of this form syntactic tautologies. Such lemmas are (mostly) useless and sometimes introduced unintentionally when proving basic facts using `rfl`, when elaboration results in a different term than the user intended. You should check that the declaration really says what you think it does." }

their value, and allow arguments starting with `_` to be unused.

{
  test := fun declName => do
    let __do_lift ← Batteries.Tactic.Lint.isAutoDecl declName
    if __do_lift = true then pure none
      else do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.isProjectionFn declName
        if __do_lift = true then pure none
          else do
            let info ← Lean.getConstInfo declName
            have ty : Lean.Expr := info.type
            have __do_jp : Lean.Expr → Lean.MetaM (Option Lean.MessageData) := fun val =>
              if (val.hasSorry || ty.hasSorry) = true then pure none
              else
                Lean.Meta.forallTelescope ty fun args ty =>
                  have e := (Lean.mkAppN val args).headBeta;
                  do
                  let ldecls ← Array.mapM Lean.Meta.getFVarLocalDecl args
                  have e : Lean.Expr := Lean.mkApp e ty
                  let __s ←
                    forIn ldecls e fun ldecl __s =>
                        have e := __s;
                        have e := Lean.mkApp e ldecl.type;
                        match ldecl.value? with
                        | some val =>
                          have e := Lean.mkApp e val;
                          pure (ForInStep.yield e)
                        | x => pure (ForInStep.yield e)
                  have e : Lean.Expr := __s
                  have usedFVars : Lean.FVarIdSet := (Lean.collectFVars { } e).fvarSet
                  have unused : Array (Lean.LocalDecl × ℕ) :=
                    Array.filter
                      (fun x =>
                        match x with
                        | (ldecl, snd) =>
                          (!ldecl.userName.isInternal ||
                              ldecl.binderInfo.isInstImplicit && ldecl.userName.hasMacroScopes) &&
                            !Std.TreeSet.contains usedFVars ldecl.fvarId)
                      ldecls.zipIdx
                  if unused.isEmpty = true then pure none
                    else
                      have msg :=
                        Lean.toMessageData unused.size ++ Lean.toMessageData " unused argument" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData (if unused.size = 1 then "" else "s") ++
                          Lean.toMessageData ":";
                      do
                      let __s ←
                        forIn unused msg fun x __s =>
                            have msg := __s;
                            match x with

doc:
Finds theorems whose bodies were elaborated in the current infotrees and whose (full)
declaration names satisfy `nameFilter`. Checks their type to see if it contains instance hypotheses
that (1) are unused in the remainder of the type (2) have types which satisfy `instanceTypeFilter`.
(Note: `instanceTypeFilter` is non-monadic, and may encounter bound variables in its argument. This
is a performance optimization. `isAppOrForallOfConstP` may be useful in detecting constant
applications and types of the form `∀ (...), bar ..` here.)

If any such parameters are found in the type of a theorem `foo`, we create a telescope in which the
types and free variables of the unused parameters are available as
`unusedParams : Array Parameter := #[p₁, p₂, ..., pₙ]`, as well as the theorem `thm : ConstantVal`
and current infotree `t`, and run `log t thm unusedParams`.

A simple pattern is therefore
```
fun _ thm unusedParams => do
  logLint linter.fooLinter (← getRef) m!"\
    {thm.name.unusedInstancesMsg unusedParams}\n\n\
    <extra caption>"
```
which logs
```null
`{foo}` has the hypothes(is/es):
  • {p₁}
  • {p₂}
  ⋮
  • {pₙ}
which (is/are) not used in the remainder of the type.

<extra caption>

Note: This linter can be disabled with `set_option {linter.fooLinter.name} false`
```
pluralizing as appropriate.

    Lean.Elab.InfoTree →
      Lean.ConstantVal →
        Array Mathlib.Linter.UnusedInstancesInType.Parameter✝ → Lean.Elab.TermElabM Unit)
  (declFilter : Lean.ConstantVal → Bool := fun x => true) : Lean.Elab.Command.CommandElabM Unit

  let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.getInfoTrees

      have thms : List Lean.ConstantVal :=
        List.filter
          (fun thm => declFilter thm && Lean.Expr.hasInstanceBinderOf instanceTypeFilter thm.type)
          (t.getTheorems __do_lift)
      if thms.isEmpty = true then pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        else do

doc:
Enter foralls recursively, creating a telescope for binders which are instances of concern
and instantiating all other bvars with `sorry`. The only free variables therefore arise from
instances of concern which we want to track the usage of.

By instantiating ordinary binders with `sorry`, `collectFVarsOutsideOfProofs` can use the
computed field accessed by `hasFVar` (in constant time) to avoid traversing any subexpressions
that do not contain a free variable for an instance of concern, which helps performance.

Used fvarIds (i.e., instances of concern) are recorded in the `StateRefT`'s `FVarIdSet`; the
returned `Array InstanceOfConcern` records all instances of concern that have been introduced,
used or not.

doc:
Gathers instance hypotheses in the type of `decl` that are unused in the remainder of the type and
whose types satisfy `p`. (Does not consider the body of the declaration.) Collects them into an
`Array Parameter`, and if (and only if) this array is nonempty, feeds it to `logOnUnused`.

Since `logOnUnused` will only be run if its argument is nonempty, it is allowed to be expensive.

Note that `p` is non-monadic, and may encounter loose bvars in its argument. This is a performance
optimization. However, the `Parameter`s are created in a telescope, and their fields will *not*
have loose bound variables.

value.text:
fun decl p logOnUnused => do
  let unusedInstances ← liftM (Lean.Expr.collectUnnecessaryInstanceBinderIdxsWhere✝ p decl.type)
  match unusedInstances.back? with
    | some maxIdx =>
      if decl.type.hasSorry = true then pure ()
      else
        Lean.Meta.forallBoundedTelescope decl.type (some (maxIdx + 1))
          (fun fvars x =>
            have unusedEverywhereInstances :=
              Lean.Expr.getUnusedForallInstanceBinderIdxsWhere p decl.type;
            do
            let unusedInstances ←
              Array.mapM
                  (fun idx => do
                    let __do_lift ← Option.mapM (fun x => liftM (Lean.Meta.inferType x)) fvars[idx]?
                    pure
                        { fvar? := fvars[idx]?, type? := __do_lift, idx := idx,
                          appearsInTypeProof := !unusedEverywhereInstances.contains idx })
                  unusedInstances
            logOnUnused unusedInstances)
          true
    | x => pure ()

doc:
Compute the parent classes of `cls`, excluding parent classes that have a parent themselves.
The reason to exclude such classes is that if there is a duplication in such a class,
then there will necessarily also be a duplication in its parent.
If `cls` carries data, then only consider parents that carry data.
If `cls` is a non-structure class, this simply returns `#[cls]`.

The resulting expressions contain bound variables that correspond to the parameters of `cls`.
The universe levels and bound variables need to be instantiated to get concrete data projections.

        Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclD `self
          (Lean.mkAppN (Lean.Expr.const cls (List.map Lean.Level.param cinfo.levelParams)) xs)
          fun inst =>
          (Mathlib.Linter.OverlappingInstances.getAbstractProjections.go✝ cls inst #[] xs
                type.isProp).run'

fun ctx lctx expectedType? =>

    (expectedType?.elim id (fun x1 x2 => Lean.Meta.forallTelescope x1 fun x x_1 => x2) do
      let overlaps ← Mathlib.Linter.OverlappingInstances.findOverlappingInstances✝
      if Std.HashMap.isEmpty overlaps = true then pure none
        else
          have overlaps := (Std.HashMap.toArray overlaps).qsort fun x1 x2 => x1.1.lt x2.1;
          have sortedOverlaps :=
            Array.foldl
              (fun s x =>
                match x with
                | (overlap, fvars) => s.alter fvars fun x => some ((x.getD #[]).push overlap))
              ∅ overlaps;
          have sortedOverlaps :=
            sortedOverlaps.toArray.qsort fun x1 x2 => x1.2.lex x2.2 Lean.Expr.lt;
          have msgs := #[];
          have needsDiamondMsg := false;
          do

            forIn sortedOverlaps (msgs, needsDiamondMsg) fun x __s =>
                have msgs := __s.1;
                have needsDiamondMsg := __s.2;

                | (fvars, overlaps) => do
                  let fvarTypes ←
                    Array.mapM
                        (fun x => do
                          let __do_lift ← x.getType

                      have msgs :=
                        msgs.push

                                Lean.toMessageData " `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr fvarTypes[0]!).sbracket ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "` instances; one is sufficient.");
                      pure (ForInStep.yield (msgs, needsDiamondMsg))
                    else do
                      let propOverlap ← Array.allM Lean.Meta.isProp overlaps

                        fun __r needsDiamondMsg =>
                        have __do_jp := fun overlaps => do
                          let __do_lift ← Lean.getLCtx
                          have localInsts : List Lean.LocalDecl :=
                            __do_lift.decls.toList.reduceOption

                            forIn fvars (redundant, __s) fun fvar __s =>
                                have redundant := __s.1;
                                have __s := __s.2;

                                | none => pure (ForInStep.done (redundant, __s))

                          have __s : Subarray Lean.Expr := __s.2

                              pure (ForInStep.yield (msgs, needsDiamondMsg))

                                Lean.MessageData.andList
                                  (List.map
                                    (fun x =>
                                      Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr x).sbracket ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData "`")

                              have overlaps :=
                                Lean.MessageData.andList
                                  (List.map
                                    (fun x =>
                                      Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr x).sbracket ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData "`")
                                    overlaps.toList);
                              have msg :=
                                Lean.toMessageData fvarTypes ++ Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadEnv m] => do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv

      Lean.PersistentHashMap.find?
        (Lean.ScopedEnvExtension.getState Lean.Parser.parserExtension env).categories `tactic with
    | some tactics =>
      have firstTokens :=
        Array.foldl
          (fun names inMods =>
            Array.foldl
              (fun names x =>
                match x with
                | (k, n) => names.insert k n)
              names inMods)
          ∅
          ((Lean.Parser.Tactic.Doc.tacticNameExt.toEnvExtension.getState env).importedEntries.push
            (Lean.Parser.Tactic.Doc.tacticNameExt.exportEntriesFn env
                (Lean.Parser.Tactic.Doc.tacticNameExt.getState env)).exported);
      have firstTokens :=
        Lean.Elab.Tactic.Doc.firstTacticTokens.addFirstTokens✝ tactics tactics.tables.leadingTable
          firstTokens;
      have firstTokens :=
        Lean.Elab.Tactic.Doc.firstTacticTokens.addFirstTokens✝ tactics tactics.tables.trailingTable
          firstTokens;
      pure firstTokens
    | x => pure ∅

fun tactics table firsts =>
  (have firsts := firsts;
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn table firsts fun x __s =>
          have firsts := __s;
          match x with
          | (tok, ps) =>
            if (tok == `«$») = true then pure (ForInStep.yield firsts)
            else do
              let __s ←
                forIn ps firsts fun x __s =>
                    have firsts := __s;
                    match x with
                    | (p, snd) => do
                      let __s ←
                        forIn (p.info.collectKinds { }) firsts fun x __s =>
                            have firsts := __s;
                            match x with
                            | (k, PUnit.unit) =>
                              if Lean.PersistentHashMap.contains tactics.kinds k = true then
                                have tok := tok.toString false;
                                have firsts :=
                                  Std.TreeMap.alter firsts k fun x => some (x.getD tok);
                                pure (ForInStep.yield firsts)
                              else pure (ForInStep.yield firsts)
                      have firsts : Lean.NameMap String := __s
                      pure (ForInStep.yield firsts)
              have firsts : Lean.NameMap String := __s
              pure (ForInStep.yield firsts)
    have firsts : Lean.NameMap String := __s
    pure firsts).run

doc:
`#allow_unused_tactic` takes as input a space-separated list of identifiers.
These identifiers are then allowed by the unused tactic linter:
even if these tactics do not modify goals, there will be no warning emitted.

Note: for this to work, these identifiers should be the `SyntaxNodeKind` of each tactic.

For instance, you can allow the `done` and `skip` tactics using
```lean
#allow_unused_tactic Lean.Parser.Tactic.done Lean.Parser.Tactic.skip
```

This change is file-local.  If you want a *persistent* change, then use the `!`-flag:
the command `#allow_unused_tactic! ids` makes the change the linter continues to ignore these
tactics also in files importing a file where this command is issued.

The command `#show_kind tac` may help to find the `SyntaxNodeKind`.

doc:
Parses the literal symbol.

The symbol is automatically included in the set of reserved tokens ("keywords").
Keywords cannot be used as identifiers, unless the identifier is otherwise escaped.
For example, `"fun"` reserves `fun` as a keyword; to refer an identifier named `fun` one can write `«fun»`.
Adding a `&` prefix prevents it from being reserved, for example `&"true"`.

Whitespace before or after the atom is used as a pretty printing hint.
For example, `" + "` parses `+` and pretty prints it with whitespace on both sides.
The whitespace has no effect on parsing behavior.

Parses a literal symbol. The `&` prefix prevents it from being included in the set of reserved tokens ("keywords").
This means that the symbol can still be recognized as an identifier by other parsers.

Some syntax categories, such as `tactic`, automatically apply `&` to the first symbol.

Whitespace before or after the atom is used as a pretty printing hint.
For example, `" + "` parses `+` and pretty prints it with whitespace on both sides.
The whitespace has no effect on parsing behavior.

(Not exposed by parser description syntax:
If the `includeIdent` argument is true, lets `ident` be reinterpreted as `atom` if it matches.)

doc:
- `unicode("→", "->")` parses a symbol matching either `→` or `->`. Each symbol is reserved.
  The second symbol is an ASCII version of the first.
  The  `pp.unicode` option controls which is used when pretty printing.
- `unicode("→", "->", preserveForPP)` is the same except for pretty printing behavior.
  When the `pp.unicode` option is enabled, then the pretty printer uses whichever symbol
  matches the underlying atom in the syntax.
  The intent is that `preserveForPP` means that the ASCII variant is preferred.
  For example, `fun` notation uses `preserveForPP` for its arrow; the delaborator chooses
  `↦` or `=>` depending on the value of `pp.unicode.fun`, letting users opt-in to formatting with `↦`.
  Note that `notation` creates a pretty printer preferring the ASCII version.

value.text:
{
  run :=
    Lean.withSetOptionIn fun stx => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Linter.getLinterOptions
      let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.Elab.getInfoState
      if
            (Lean.Linter.getLinterValue Mathlib.Linter.linter.unusedTactic __do_lift &&
                __do_lift_1.enabled) =
              true then
          do
          let __do_lift ← get
          if __do_lift.messages.hasErrors = true then pure ()
            else
              if stx.isOfKind `Mathlib.Linter.UnusedTactic.«command#show_kind_» = true then pure ()
              else do
                let env ← Lean.getEnv
                have cats : Lean.Parser.ParserCategories :=
                  (Lean.ScopedEnvExtension.getState Lean.Parser.parserExtension env).categories
                match
                    Lean.Parser.ParserCategory.kinds <$>
                      Lean.PersistentHashMap.find? cats `tactic with
                  | some tactics =>
                    match
                      Lean.Parser.ParserCategory.kinds <$>
                        Lean.PersistentHashMap.find? cats `conv with
                    | some convs => do
                      let trees ← Lean.Elab.getInfoTrees
                      let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get Mathlib.Linter.UnusedTactic.allowedRef
                      have exceptions : Std.HashSet Lean.SyntaxNodeKind :=
                        __do_lift.union
                          (Mathlib.Linter.UnusedTactic.allowedUnusedTacticExt.getState env)

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadEnv m] [Lean.MonadFileMap m] pos => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
  have drs : Lean.NameMap Lean.DeclarationRanges :=
    Lean.declRangeExt.getState __do_lift Lean.EnvExtension.AsyncMode.local
  let fm ← Lean.getFileMap
  have nms : Array Lean.Ident := #[]

    forIn drs nms fun x __s =>
        have nms := __s;
        match x with
        | (nm, rgs) =>
          if pos ≤ fm.ofPosition rgs.range.pos then
            have ofPos1 := fm.ofPosition rgs.selectionRange.pos;
            have ofPos2 := fm.ofPosition rgs.selectionRange.endPos;

          else pure (ForInStep.yield nms)

Return the name of the option being set, if any.

The `setOption` linter: this lints any `set_option` command, term or tactic
which sets a `debug`, `pp`, `profiler` or `trace` option.
This also warns if an option containing `maxHeartbeats` (typically, the `maxHeartbeats` or
`synthInstance.maxHeartbeats` option) or the `linter.flexible` or
`backward.inferInstanceAs.wrap.reuseSubInstances ` option is set.

**Why is this bad?** The `debug`, `pp`, `profiler` and `trace` options are good for debugging,
but should not be used in production code.

`maxHeartbeats` options should be scoped as `set_option opt in ...` (and be followed by a comment
explaining the need for them; another linter enforces this).
The `linter.flexible` option should be scoped as `set_option opt in ...`.

**How to fix this?** The `maxHeartbeats` and `linter.flexible` option changes can be scoped to
individual commands, if they are truly necessary.
New `backward.inferInstanceAs.wrap.reuseSubInstances` instances are technical debt,
and should not be introduced.

The `debug`, `pp`, `profiler` and `trace` are usually not necessary for production code,
so you can simply remove them. (Some tests will intentionally use one of these options;
in this case, simply allow the linter.)

{

    Lean.withSetOptionIn fun stx => do

Check `name` is a `Name` containing an underscore that should be linted against
by the `defsWithUnderscore` linter. Namely, we do not lint
* names ending in an underscore, or in a namespace ending with an underscore,
* names containing guillemets `«»` (these tend to be `term<something>` declarations,
  i.e. internal names for notation, not user-facing commands),
* names with a component starting with `term` (e.g. `Nat.term_!`)
* names starting with `Mathlib.Tactic`, `Parser` or containing a `Simps` component
  (these are probably custom simps projections, i.e. affect how `simps` names its auto-generated
  lemmas: we usually prefer a generated name `coe_support` over `coeSupport`, which requires a
  projection named `coe_support`)
* names that end in `_<number>` or in `_mathlib` (these tend to be autogenerated instance names),
* library notes.

fun name =>
  (have s := name.toString;
    have declName := name;
    have last := (declName.components.getLast?.getD `Default).toString;
    if
        (((last.endsWith '_' || s.contains '«' ||
                            declName.components.any fun x => x.toString.startsWith "term") ||
                          `LibraryNote.isPrefixOf declName ||
                        `Mathlib.Tactic.isPrefixOf declName ||
                      `Parser.isPrefixOf declName ||
                    declName.components.any fun x => x == `Simps) ||
                  last.endsWith "_1" ||
                last.endsWith "_2" ||
              last.endsWith "_mathlib" ||
            declName.components.any fun x => x.toString.endsWith '_') =
          true then
      pure false
    else if declName.toString.contains "_" = true then pure true else pure false).run

doc:
The "longFile" linter emits a warning on files which are longer than a certain number of lines
(`linter.style.longFileDefValue` by default on mathlib, no limit for downstream projects).
If this option is set to `N` lines, the linter warns once a file has more than `N` lines.
A value of `0` silences the linter entirely.

{
  run :=
    Lean.withSetOptionIn fun stx => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
      have linterBound : ℕ := Lean.Option.get __do_lift Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longFile
      if (linterBound == 0) = true then pure ()
        else do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
          have defValue : ℕ :=
            Lean.Option.get __do_lift Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longFileDefValue
          let smallOption : Prop :=
            have __discr := stx;
            if __discr.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Command.set_option = true then
              have __discr_1 := __discr.getArg 0;
              have __discr_2 := __discr.getArg 1;
              if __discr_2.matchesIdent `linter.style.longFile = true then
                have __discr_3 := __discr.getArg 2;
                if __discr_3.matchesNull 0 = true then
                  have __discr := __discr.getArg 3;
                  have x := { raw := __discr };
                  { raw := x.raw }.getNat ≤ defValue
                else
                  have __discr_4 := __discr.getArg 2;
                  have __discr := __discr.getArg 3;
                  false = true
              else
                have __discr_3 := __discr.getArg 1;
                have __discr_4 := __discr.getArg 2;
                have __discr := __discr.getArg 3;
                false = true
            else
              have __discr := stx;
              false = true
          if smallOption then
              Mathlib.Linter.logLint0Disable Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longFile stx
                (Lean.toMessageData "The default value of the `longFile` linter is " ++
                            Lean.toMessageData defValue ++
                          Lean.toMessageData ".\nThe current value of " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData linterBound ++
                      Lean.toMessageData
                        " does not exceed the allowed bound.\nPlease, remove the `set_option linter.style.longFile " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData linterBound ++
                  Lean.toMessageData "`.")
            else
              if Lean.Parser.isTerminalCommand stx = true then do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getMainModule
                if (__do_lift == `Mathlib) = true then pure ()
                  else
                    match stx.getTailPos? with
                    | some init => do
                      let __do_lift ← Lean.getFileMap
                      have lastLine : ℕ := (__do_lift.toPosition init).line
                      if
                            (decide (lastLine ≤ defValue) && decide (defValue < linterBound)) =
                              true then
                          Mathlib.Linter.logLint0Disable Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longFile stx
                            (Lean.toMessageData "The default value of the `longFile` linter is " ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData defValue ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData ".\nThis file is " ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData lastLine ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                    " lines long which does not exceed the allowed bound.\nPlease, remove the `set_option linter.style.longFile " ++
                                Lean.toMessageData linterBound ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "`.")
                        else
                          have candidate := lastLine / 100 * 100 + 200;
                          have candidate := max candidate defValue;
                          if
                              (decide (defValue ≤ linterBound) && decide (linterBound < lastLine)) =
                                true then
                            Mathlib.Linter.logLint0Disable Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longFile stx
                              (Lean.toMessageData "This file is " ++ Lean.toMessageData lastLine ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData " lines long, but the limit is " ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData linterBound ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData
                                      ".\n\nYou can extend the allowed length of the file using `set_option linter.style.longFile " ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData candidate ++
                                Lean.toMessageData
                                  "`.\nYou can completely disable this linter by setting the length limit to `0`.")
                          else
                            if
                                (linterBound == candidate || linterBound + 100 == candidate) =
                                  true then
                              pure ()
                            else
                              Mathlib.Linter.logLint0Disable Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longFile
                                stx
                                (Lean.toMessageData "This file is " ++
                                                Lean.toMessageData lastLine ++
                                              Lean.toMessageData
                                                " lines long. The current limit is " ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData linterBound ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData ", but it is expected to be " ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData candidate ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData ":\n`set_option linter.style.longFile " ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData candidate ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData "`.")
                    | x => pure ()
              else pure (),
  name :=
    ((((((((((Lean.Name.anonymous.mkStr "_private").mkStr "Mathlib").mkStr "Tactic").mkStr
                                  "Linter").mkStr
                              "Style").mkNum
                          0).mkStr
                      "Mathlib").mkStr
                  "Linter").mkStr
              "Style").mkStr
          "longFile").mkStr
      "longFileLinter" }

doc:
The `whitespace` linter emits a warning if
* either a command does not start at the beginning of a line;
* or the "hypotheses segment" of a declaration does not coincide with its pretty-printed version.

In practice, this makes sure that the spacing in a typical declaration looks like
```lean
example (a : Nat) {R : Type} [Add R] : <not linted part>
```
as opposed to
```lean
example (a: Nat) {R:Type}  [Add  R] : <not linted part>
```

{

    Lean.withSetOptionIn fun stx => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Linter.getLinterOptions
      if Lean.Linter.getLinterValue Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.whitespace __do_lift = true then do
          let __do_lift ← get

            else
              if (stx.find? fun x => x.isOfKind `Lean.runCmd).isSome = true then pure ()
              else
                have __do_jp := fun __r =>
                  if
                      (stx.find? fun x => x.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Command.macro_rules).isSome =
                        true then
                    pure ()
                  else

                    | some upTo => do
                      let fmt ←
                        tryCatch

                              (some <$> Lean.PrettyPrinter.ppCategory `command stx))
                            fun x => do
                            Lean.Linter.logLintIf Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.whitespace.verbose
                                (stx.getHead?.getD stx)
                                (Lean.toMessageData
                                  "The `whitespace` linter had some parsing issues: feel free to silence it and report this error!")
                            pure none
                      match fmt with
                        | some fmt =>
                          have st := fmt.pretty;
                          have origSubstring := stx.getSubstring?.getD default;
                          have orig := origSubstring.toString;
                          have scan := Mathlib.Linter.parallelScan✝ orig st;
                          have docStringEnd :=
                            (stx.find? fun x => x.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Command.docComment).getD
                              default;
                          have docStringEnd := docStringEnd.getTailPos?.getD default;
                          have forbidden :=
                            Mathlib.Linter.Style.Whitespace.getUnlintedRanges✝
                              Mathlib.Linter.Style.Whitespace.unlintedNodes✝ ∅ stx;
                          do
                          let __s ←
                            forIn scan (none, ()) fun s __s =>
                                have center :=
                                  origSubstring.stopPos.unoffsetBy
                                    (Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.srcEndPos✝ s);
                                have rg :=
                                  { start := center,
                                    stop :=
                                      ((center.offsetBy
                                                (Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.srcEndPos✝
                                                  s)).unoffsetBy
                                            (Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.srcStartPos✝ s)).increaseBy
                                        1 };
                                if
                                    (Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.msg✝ s).startsWith "Oh no" =
                                      true then
                                  do
                                  Lean.Linter.logLintIf
                                      Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.whitespace.verbose
                                      (Lean.Syntax.ofRange rg)
                                      (Lean.toMessageData
                                        "This should not have happened: please report this issue!")
                                  Lean.Linter.logLintIf
                                      Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.whitespace.verbose
                                      (Lean.Syntax.ofRange rg)
                                      (Lean.toMessageData "Formatted string:\n" ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData fmt ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData "\nOriginal string:\n" ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData origSubstring)

                                        have srcWindow :=

                                            (Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.srcNat✝ s)
                                            (ctx + Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.length✝ s);
                                        have expectedWindow :=

                                            (Mathlib.Linter.FormatError.fmtPos✝ s) (ctx + 1);
                                        do

                                            (Lean.Syntax.ofRange rg)

                                                      Lean.toMessageData
                                                        " in the source\n\nThis part of the code\n  '" ++
                                                    Lean.toMessageData srcWindow ++
                                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                                    "'\nshould be written as\n  '" ++
                                                Lean.toMessageData expectedWindow ++
                                              Lean.toMessageData "'\n")

                                            Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.whitespace.verbose
                                            (Lean.Syntax.ofRange rg)
                                            (Lean.toMessageData "Formatted string:\n" ++

                                    else pure (ForInStep.done (some (), ()))
                                  else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))

doc:
`mkWindow orig start ctx` extracts from `orig` a string that starts at the first
non-whitespace character before `start`, then expands to cover `ctx` more characters
and continues still until the first non-whitespace character.

In essence, it extracts the substring of `orig` that begins at `start`, continues for `ctx`
characters plus expands left and right until it encounters the first whitespace character,

doc:
Parse an infotree to find all the sequences of tactics contained within `stx`.

We consider a sequence here to be a maximal interval of tactics joined by `;` or newlines.
This function returns an array of sequences. For example, a proof of the form:
```
by
  tac1
  · tac2; tac3
  · tac4; tac5
```
would result in three sequences:
* `#[tac1, (· tac2; tac3), (· tac4; tac5)]`
* `#[tac2, tac3]`
* `#[tac4, tac5]`

Similarly, a declaration with multiple `by` blocks results in each of the blocks getting its
own sequence.

value.text:
fun tree => do
  let ctx ← read
  let state ← get
  have ctxInfo : Lean.Elab.ContextInfo :=
    { env := state.env, fileMap := ctx.fileMap, ngen := state.ngen }
  let out ←
    Lean.Elab.InfoTree.visitM (fun x x_1 x_2 => pure true)
        (fun ctx i _c cs =>
          have relevantChildren := (List.filterMap id cs).toArray;
          have childTactics := Array.filterMap Prod.fst relevantChildren;
          have childSequences := (Array.map Prod.snd relevantChildren).flatten;
          have stx := i.stx;
          if
              stx.getKind ∈
                [`Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq, `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq1Indented,
                  `Lean.Parser.Term.byTactic] then
            pure
              (none,
                if childTactics.isEmpty = true then childSequences
                else childSequences.push childTactics)
          else
            match stx.getHeadInfo? with
            | some (Lean.SourceInfo.original leading pos trailing endPos) =>
              if stx.getKind ∈ [`«;», `Lean.cdotTk, `«]», Lean.nullKind, `by] then
                pure (none, childSequences)
              else
                if stx.getKind ∈ [`Lean.Parser.Tactic.withAnnotateState] then
                  pure (childTactics[0]?, childSequences)
                else
                  match i with
                  | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTacticInfo i =>
                    have childSequences :=
                      if
                          stx.getKind ∈
                            [`Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticTry_, `Lean.Parser.Tactic.anyGoals] then
                        Array.map
                          (fun x =>
                            Array.map (fun i => { ctxI := i.ctxI, tacI := i.tacI, mayFail := true })
                              x)
                          childSequences
                      else childSequences;
                    pure (some { ctxI := ctx, tacI := i, mayFail := false }, childSequences)
                  | x => pure (none, childSequences)
            | x => pure (none, childSequences))
        (some ctxInfo) tree
  pure ((Option.map Prod.snd out).getD #[])

doc:
Test the `config` against a sequence of tactics, using the context info and tactic info
from the start of the sequence.

value.text:
fun config tacticSeq i ctx =>
  Lean.withRef (Lean.mkNullNode (Lean.TSyntaxArray.raw tacticSeq)) do
    let stx ←
      do
        let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
        let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
        let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
        pure
            {
              raw :=
                Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.seq1
                  (Lean.Syntax.node info `null
                    (#[].append (Lean.Syntax.TSepArray.ofElems tacticSeq).elemsAndSeps)) }
    match i.tacI.goalsBefore with
      | [goal] => do
        let __x ←
          Lean.withHeartbeats do
              let e ←
                tryCatch
                    (do
                      let r ← i.runTacticCode goal stx.raw
                      ExceptT.run (pure r))
                    fun e =>
                    have __do_jp := fun __r => EarlyReturnT.return [goal];
                    if (!i.mayFail) = true then do
                      let __r ←
                        Lean.logWarning
                            (Lean.toMessageData "original tactic '" ++ Lean.toMessageData stx ++
                                Lean.toMessageData "' failed: " ++
                              Lean.toMessageData e.toMessageData)
                      __do_jp __r
                    else __do_jp ()
              EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r
        match __x with
          | (oldGoals, oldHeartbeats) => do
            let __x ← Lean.withHeartbeats (config.test i.ctxI i.tacI ctx goal)
            match __x with
              | (new, newHeartbeats) => do
                let __do_lift ← config.tell stx.raw oldGoals oldHeartbeats new newHeartbeats
                match __do_lift with
                  | some msg => Lean.logWarning msg
                  | x => pure ()
      | x => pure ()

We say a variable `x` is "relevant" if
- It occurs in the `toPreserve` array, or

- If `indirectProps` is true, `x` is a local declaration and its value mentions a relevant variable `y`.

fun modifiers stx =>
  have declKind := stx.getKind;
  do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Command.getScope
  have modifiers : Lean.Elab.Modifiers :=
    if
        (modifiers.computeKind == Lean.Elab.ComputeKind.regular && __do_lift.isMeta &&
              declKind != `Lean.Parser.Command.theorem &&
            declKind != `Lean.Parser.Command.example) =
          true then
      { stx := modifiers.stx, docString? := modifiers.docString?,
        visibility := modifiers.visibility, isProtected := modifiers.isProtected,
        computeKind := Lean.Elab.ComputeKind.meta, recKind := modifiers.recKind,
        isUnsafe := modifiers.isUnsafe, attrs := modifiers.attrs }
    else modifiers
  if (declKind == `Lean.Parser.Command.abbrev) = true then
      pure (Lean.Elab.Command.mkDefViewOfAbbrev modifiers stx)
    else
      if (declKind == `Lean.Parser.Command.definition) = true then
        pure (Lean.Elab.Command.mkDefViewOfDef modifiers stx)
      else
        if (declKind == `Lean.Parser.Command.theorem) = true then
          pure (Lean.Elab.Command.mkDefViewOfTheorem modifiers stx)
        else
          if (declKind == `Lean.Parser.Command.opaque) = true then
            Lean.Elab.Command.mkDefViewOfOpaque modifiers stx
          else
            if (declKind == `Lean.Parser.Command.instance) = true then
              Lean.Elab.Command.mkDefViewOfInstance modifiers stx
            else
              if (declKind == `Lean.Parser.Command.example) = true then
                pure (Lean.Elab.Command.mkDefViewOfExample modifiers stx)
              else Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "unexpected kind of definition")

    have __do_jp := fun val =>
      pure

          headerRef := Lean.mkNullNode ↑(Std.Rio.Sliceable.mkSlice stx.getArgs *...3),

          value := val, docString? := modifiers.docString? };
    match stx[3].getOptional? with
    | some val => do

    | none =>
      have __do_jp := fun val => do
        let val ←

            let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos

            let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext

                      (Lean.Syntax.atom info "default_or_ofNonempty%")

          do

            let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
            let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext

fun modifiers stx => do
  let attrKind ← Lean.Elab.liftMacroM (Lean.Elab.toAttributeKind stx[0])
  let prio ← Lean.Elab.liftMacroM (Lean.Elab.expandOptNamedPrio stx[2])
  let attrStx ←
    do
      let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
      let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
      let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
      pure
          {
            raw :=
              Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.Parser.Attr.instance (Lean.Syntax.atom info "instance")
                (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `null (Lean.quote prio).raw) }
  have modifiers : Lean.Elab.Modifiers :=
    modifiers.addAttr { kind := attrKind, name := `instance, stx := attrStx.raw }
  match Lean.Elab.expandDeclSig stx[4] with
    | (binders, type) =>
      have __do_jp := fun declId =>
        pure
          { kind := Lean.Elab.DefKind.instance, ref := stx,
            headerRef := Lean.mkNullNode ↑(Std.Rio.Sliceable.mkSlice stx.getArgs *...5),
            modifiers := modifiers, declId := declId, binders := binders, type? := some type,
            value := stx[5], docString? := modifiers.docString? };
      match stx[3].getOptional? with
      | some declId => do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor `Elab.instance.mkInstanceName
        have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Command.CommandElabM Lean.Elab.DefView := fun __r => do
          let declId ← pure declId
          __do_jp declId
        if __do_lift = true then do
            let id ← Lean.Elab.Command.mkInstanceName binders.getArgs type
            have cls : Lean.Name := `Elab.instance.mkInstanceName
            let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
            if __do_lift = true then do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getCurrNamespace
                let __r ←
                  Lean.addTrace cls
                      (Lean.toMessageData "generated " ++ Lean.toMessageData (__do_lift ++ id) ++
                          Lean.toMessageData " for " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData declId)
                __do_jp __r
              else __do_jp ()
          else __do_jp ()
      | none => do
        let id ← Lean.Elab.Command.mkInstanceName binders.getArgs type
        have cls : Lean.Name := `Elab.instance.mkInstanceName
        let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
        have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Command.CommandElabM Lean.Elab.DefView := fun __r => do
          let declId ←
            pure
                (Lean.mkNode `Lean.Parser.Command.declId
                    #[(Lean.mkIdentFrom stx[1] id true).raw, Lean.mkNullNode]).raw
          __do_jp declId
        if __do_lift = true then do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.getCurrNamespace
            let __r ←
              Lean.addTrace cls
                  (Lean.toMessageData "generated " ++ Lean.toMessageData (__do_lift ++ id))
            __do_jp __r
          else __do_jp ()

fun cmd => do
  let ns ← Lean.getCurrNamespace
  let id1 ← Mathlib.Command.MinImports.getId cmd
  have id2 : Lean.Ident :=
    Lean.mkIdentFrom id1 (Mathlib.Command.MinImports.previousInstName id1.getId)
  match cmd.find? fun x => x.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Command.declaration with
    | some declStx =>
      match declStx.find? fun x => x.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Command.declModifiers with
      | some modifiersStx =>
        have modifiers := { raw := modifiersStx };
        do
        let s ← get
        let modifiers ← Lean.Elab.elabModifiers modifiers
        set s
        Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM
            ((have shortName := id1.getId;
              have view := Lean.extractMacroScopes shortName;
              have name := view.name;
              have isRootName := `_root_.isPrefixOf name;
              have fullName :=
                if isRootName = true then
                  { name := name.replacePrefix `_root_ Lean.Name.anonymous,
                      imported := view.imported, ctx := view.ctx, scopes := view.scopes }.review
                else ns ++ shortName;
              match modifiers.visibility with
              | Lean.Elab.Visibility.private => do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
                pure (Lean.mkPrivateName __do_lift fullName)
              | x => pure fullName) <|>
              Lean.realizeGlobalConstNoOverload id1 <|>
                Lean.realizeGlobalConstNoOverload id2.raw <|> pure (ns ++ id1.getId))
      | x => pure default
    | x => pure default

`previousInstName nm` takes as input a name `nm`, assuming that it is the name of an
auto-generated "nameless" `instance`.
If `nm` ends in `..._n`, where `n` is a number, it returns the same name, but with `_n` replaced

fun x =>
  match x with
  | nm@h:(init.str tail) =>
    have last := tail.takeEndWhile fun x => x != '_';
    have newTail :=
      match last.toNat? with
      | some n.succ.succ => toString "_" ++ toString (n + 1)
      | x => "";
    have newTailPrefix := tail.dropEndWhile fun x => x != '_';
    if newTailPrefix.isEmpty = true then nm
    else
      have newTail :=
        (if (newTailPrefix.back == '_') = true then newTailPrefix.dropEnd 1
            else newTailPrefix).copy ++
          newTail;
      init.str newTail
  | nm => nm
